headline: OpenAI says it fired three safety researchers for breaking its rules on sensitive information, while the researchers say they were punished for raising safety concerns.
score_reason: Viral floor 9: about 45 outlets carry it (VIRAL RULE, Rafi, 10 Oct 2026); curator score was 6
importance_line: People who rely on AI labs to be open about risks have reason to watch whether safety staff can speak up and work with outside evaluators, but each side's account is its own and OpenAI has not said what the alleged breach was.
summary: NPR reports that OpenAI says it fired safety researchers Mikita Balesni, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang for violating policies on handling sensitive information, while the three say in a letter published on 8 October 2026 that the firings were a pretext to punish them for speaking up about safety and working with outside researchers. In its reply on Friday 9 October, which Business Insider reports, OpenAI said an internal investigation found a "significant breach of trust" beyond what the letter described and denied that the firings were about raising safety concerns; this answers the dispute we carried in our 9 Oct edition from TechCrunch, and neither side's claims have been independently verified.
notes: Reuters original blocked; read NPR, Business Insider and Yahoo Finance UK. Reply story: names the 9 Oct edition TechCrunch item on the researchers' dispute.
